title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1LC0RE_1LD1LB_1LA1LD_1RF0RA_---1RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1LC0RE_1LD1LB_1LA1LD_1RF0RA_---1RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Each sweep of the head turns the period-3 background into its complement (010 ↔ 101, 100 ↔ 011, 001 ↔ 110; six shift rules proved in Lean). Read when the head is at the right end in state B, the tape is (100)^x 1011 (010)^a1 11 (010)^a2 11 … (010)^n 01: the last block n loses 2 copies per visit, the inner blocks lose 4, 4, 12, 20, … (one block stays at 100 or 120 for a long time), new blocks appear behind the front counter x, which often doubles or drops by 5 from one visit to the next like a binary counter. When the last block is used up, 120 1101 turns into a new last block of 119. No closed map yet.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 83,871 cells have been visited and 30,719 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.463). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.047).

claims.title: Complementing shift rules
claims.text: C, A and D cross (010)^n, (100)^n, (001)^n to the left and B, E, A cross (110)^n, (101)^n, (011)^n to the right, 3n steps each, for every n.

claims.title: No halt in the first 3·10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: A plain C simulator (longrun.c, on tools/c/tm.h) runs 3·1010 steps from blank tape without a halt; at the end the head has visited cells -628,527 to 98 and 334,129 cells hold a 1.

claims.title: The list at the right-end visits
claims.text: Read off the direct run to 3·10<sup>7</sup> steps: the last block goes 54, 52, 50, … (minus 2 per visit); a block of 100 (later 120) sits in front of it for many visits while the blocks before it shrink by 4, 4, 12, 20; the front counter runs 245, 490, 485, 970, 965 (doubling and subtracting 5 in turn) and moves differently when a new block is born

claims.title: Deterministic counter, no sign of a halt
claims.text: The front counter behaves much like a binary counter (double, or subtract 5) and every other count moves by fixed amounts per visit; nothing points to the halting transition (F reading 0) being reached.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The block list is understood one visit at a time; the front counter and the birth of new blocks have not been reduced to a map.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Each sweep of the head flips the repeating pattern of the tape into its complement; underneath, a list of blocks shrinks at fixed rates while a counter at the front doubles and feeds new blocks into the list.

facts.text: The complementing sweeps, proved for every length.
The last block of the list at each right-end visit.
No halt in the C simulator.

sections.heading: Complementing sweeps over a list
html: The background has period 3, and every pass of the head turns it into its complement: 010 becomes 101 going left and back again going right. Read at the moments the head is at the right end in state B, the tape is a list:

The last block shrinks by 2 per visit, the block of 120 waits, the blocks before it shrink by 4 or 12 or more, and the front counter often doubles or drops by 5, pushing a new block into the list from time to time. How the front counter and the new blocks are tied together is the next thing to work out.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.463). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.047).
After 109 steps the tape spans 83,871 cells (62,156 left of the start, 67 right), with a density of 1s of 0.366.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: Complementing sweeper on a list of (010)^n blocks with a doubling front counter
summary: Sweeps alternately complement the period-3 background; at the right end the list (100)^x 1011 [(010)^a 11]* (010)^n 01 has its last block shrinking by 2 per sweep and the inner blocks by multiples of 4, while the front counter x roughly doubles or drops by 5 and feeds new blocks into the list.
